title: Routes, Params & Nesting
body:
# Routes, Params & Nesting

## The table drives the app

```ts
const routes = [
  { path: '/', name: 'dashboard', component: Dashboard },
  { path: '/rust/:module/:lesson', name: 'rust-lesson', component: LessonView },
  { path: '/project/:id', component: ProjectView, props: true },
  { path: '/settings', component: SettingsView },
  { path: '/rust/:module', redirect: to => `/rust/${to.params.module}/intro` }
]
```

`props: true` passes params as props → components stay router-agnostic and
testable.

## Nested views

```ts
{ path: '/project/:id', component: ProjectLayout,
  children: [
    { path: '', component: Overview },
    { path: 'files', component: FilesTab }
  ]}
```

The parent renders `<router-view>`; children swap inside it. URL stays the
single source of truth for deep-linking — exactly how this app's lesson
workspace encodes `track/module/lesson`.

## Reacting to param changes

```ts
const lesson = computed(() =>
  findLesson(route.params.module, route.params.lesson)
)
watch(lesson, loadWorkspace)   // same component instance persists across params!
```

Route changes with shared components do NOT remount by default — watch params
(see `LessonView.vue`).

## Hash vs history mode
Desktop apps under `tauri://` use **hash history** (`createWebHashHistory`) —
no server rewrites needed. That's this app's choice.
